newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power mixed amid mild weather outlook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power mixed amid mild weather outlook.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. Thursday were mixed compared with Tuesday's levels on outlook of weather in the region moderating from recent lows.
"As we head into the weekend, temperatures are going to moderate," said one Midwest trader.
Although much of Midwest would experience more seasonal temperatures, very northern sections of Minnesota, Wisconsin and North Dakota would stay very cold.
Volume of trading was thin as many participants scheduled their power needs this week before the Christmas holiday, said market sources.
"A lot of people bought what they need for the month," said another Midwest trader.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak, non-firm power prices for Friday delivery were discussed in the $17.50-$19.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) area, a wider quote than Tuesday's $18.75-20.00 for Thursday delivery.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power for Friday was pegged a $11.50-$12.50, slightly firmer than Tuesday's $11.00.
A 420 megawatt (MW) Big Stone coal-fired generating plant in South Dakota was shut today for repairs, and expected to stay off line at least for a couple of days.
Power output at the 538 MW Duane Arnold nuclear station in Palo, Iowa, was reduced after a recirculation pump tripped.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Friday were valued at $17.50-$20.00, stronger than Tuesday's $16.50-17.50 range for Thursday.
MAIN off peak power for Friday was assessed at $10.50-$11.00, off from Tuesday's $11.50-12.50 range.

In the upper half of the Midwest, Friday temperatures were predicted to peak in 20-50 Fahrenheit degrees and bottom in the teens to the 40s. Some areas along the Canadian border would see maximum temperatures in the single digits Friday and minimum temperatures as much as 25 degrees below zero.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Friday in the $11.50-12.50 range, flat from Tuesday's day-head prices, Friday ECAR electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery was quoted at $11.00-$12.00, compared with Tuesday's $12.00.
January/February ECAR prices were notionally valued at $24.00-$25.00, compared with a quote of $25.00 Tuesday.
Friday temperatures in ECAR were expected to range in the 30s-40s during the day and teens to 30s at night.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), where temperatures were anticipated to range in the 30s-60s Friday, peak, non-firm power for Friday delivery was pegged in a $15.00-$20.00 range, up from Tuesday's $11.00-$12.00.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP for next-day delivery were assessed at $11.00-$14.00, compared with $11.75-13.00 Tuesday for Thursday.
January/February peak prices in SPP were at $23.50-$25.00, weaker bid than Tuesday's $25.00.
